prompt:
RENDER LANGUAGE (must match exactly, this is a fixed house style for this batch):
Flat 2D game asset concept, strictly orthogonal front view — no isometric, no three-quarter, no perspective, no camera tilt. Every material is rendered as FLAT POSTERIZED VALUE STEPS: distinct flat hard-edged color bands (4-5 per material — shadow / body / lit / rim), like a limited-palette indexed illustration. NOT a smooth gradient, NOT airbrushed, NOT painterly continuous blending — each band is one flat, uniform color with a hard boundary to the next band. No ink outline or contour line anywhere; bands separate from each other and from the background by color-value alone. No cast shadow, no floor plane, no backdrop scenery, no vignette, no dramatic studio lighting, no ambient occlusion gradient — the subject sits isolated on a single flat, uniformly toned dark neutral background (flat mid-dark blue-grey, no gradient in the background). Authored in its fully warm, lit-material appearance — never desaturated, never cooled, never tinted toward blue-grey (that is a separate derived state computed later, not something to render now).

Subject: a tileable game floor/wall surface, ancient amphitheatre travertine stone masonry, viewed dead-on flat (this is a material swatch, not an object — ignore the "isolated subject on dark background" instruction above and instead fill the entire frame edge-to-edge with the tiled surface).

CRITICAL FIELD RULE: the field (the main flat area of every block) must use ONLY two colors: lit face #a8876b and rim highlight #cbae8c, alternating between adjacent blocks so no two touching blocks are the same shade. Do NOT use the darker shadow tones (#5a4638, #3b2f28) or the mid body tone (#806450) as a block's main fill — those darker values are reserved for: the joint/mortar gaps between blocks, a few small crack marks, and small chipped-corner shadow accents only, never for a whole block's field color. The overall surface must read as light and pale, not medium-brown — if the image looks like a medium brown wall, it is wrong; it should look like pale sun-bleached stone.

Joints: irregular, hand-cut ashlar masonry — blocks vary in size (mix of larger and smaller blocks within the pattern, not a uniform grid), joints are slightly uneven and offset row to row (not a perfect running-bond or perfect grid), joint gap itself is a thin dark line #3b2f28 only 1-2 pixels wide conceptually (thin, not a bold border).

Surface detail: sparse hairline cracks and a few small chipped corners (revealing the paler #cbae8c beneath), rendered as small flat marks, not covering every block.

No outline weight beyond the thin joint gap itself — the blocks must not have an additional drawn contour on top of the joint.

Forbidden: any block using the dark shadow or mid-body tone as its main field color; uniform perfectly regular grid; bright/saturated color; brass/gold/metal color; glow; text/watermark; photographic realism.
